LESSON: DIVISION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.5: Division

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Division. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: When can you use division in real life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. divide up to a two-digit number by a one-digit number with and without remainder,
2. divide up to a three-digit number by 100
3. relate multiplication of numbers to division of same numbers in different situations,
4. appreciate the use of division in day-to-day life. The learner is guided to: to a two-digit number by a one-digit number without remainder using number cards or other resources, up to a two-digit number by a one-digit number with remainder and prepare division charts, up to a three-digit number by 100 and multiplication of the same numbers to establish a relationship between multiplication and division, division using digital devices. When can you use division in real life? 11

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market in your county, count 10 mangoes. Put them in 2 groups of 5. That is sorting and grouping.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row. Write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and your parent gives you 5 more, you have 12 shillings. That is addition.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Division.
2. Explain Division to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Try this activity: discuss and carry out the division of up to a two-digit number by a one-digit number without remainder using number cards or other resources,
4. Show that you can: divide up to a two-digit number by a one-digit number with and without remainder,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Division. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: When can you use division in real life?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss and carry out the division of up to a two-digit number by a one-digit number without remainder using number cards or other resources,
2. Jointly with peers, play games involving division using digital devices.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. divide up to a two-digit number by a one-digit number with and without remainder,
2. divide up to a three-digit number by 100
3. relate multiplication of numbers to division of same numbers in different situations,
4. appreciate the use of division in day-to-day life.
